/.title: U.S. federal workforce separations after the 2025 changes (OPM data)
/.problem: Can we predict how many employees each federal agency loses after a return-to-office order and a paid resignation offer?
/.situation: On 20 January 2025 the President ordered federal agencies to end remote work, and on 28 January OPM offered nearly every federal employee a deferred resignation: stop working, stay paid until 30 September 2025, then leave. The offer closed on 12 February.
/.data_used: OPM's Federal Workforce Data: every separation from federal service by month since 2005 (agency, age band, length of service, type of separation) and monthly snapshots of all 2.3 million employees, published through a public API.
/.protocol_line: Each agency's employees are simulated from the December 2024 snapshot and separation rates before 2025, with assumptions from earlier research. Later separations are scored separately; source revisions prevent a claim of information available beforehand.
/.intro: Simulates the 2.3 million civilian federal employees in OPM's data as cohort twins (one per agency, age band, length of service, appointment, schedule and supervisory status), each with its own pre-2025 separation rates by type. The return-to-office order raises voluntary leaving and the deferred resignation offer is taken up by the employees most likely to leave anyway, as a one-off early-retirement window does. Separations by agency and month from February to December 2025 are scored against what OPM recorded; the alternative asks what the return-to-office order would have done without the resignation offer.
/.world: Federal civilian employees in OPM's data, as of December 2024, grouped into cohort twins by agency, age band, length of service, appointment, work schedule and supervisory status. Separations by type follow each twin's own pre-change rates; the 2025 return-to-office order and the deferred resignation offer enter on their announced dates. Outcomes are separations by agency and month, February to December 2025.
/.source: manifests/sources.json (OPM Federal Workforce Data API, pinned file versions with SHA-256)

/results.design: In January 2025 federal agencies were ordered back to the office and offered nearly every full-time employee a paid deferred resignation. Each agency's employees are simulated from the December 2024 snapshot with separation rates from records dated before 2025 in later-revised source files; separations from February to December 2025 are the actual outcome. The same method was first checked on 2022, 2023 and 2024, years without such a change.

rto_mult.source: Employee turnover rose about 14% after return-to-office mandates at 54 large S&P 500 technology and financial firms (2020-2023), from about 3 million LinkedIn employment histories: Ding, Jin, Ma, Xing & Yang, 'Return-to-office mandates and brain drain' (working paper, reported by Fortune on 11 December 2024; the authors' summary gives 13-14%). Applied to quits and retirements from the presidential memorandum of 20 January 2025. The range is half to one and a half times the effect (authored), because federal employees face different outside options than private technology staff.

drp_window_mult.source: A one-year early-retirement window roughly doubled departures among eligible employees at a Fortune 500 firm: simulated retirements of 91.0 without the window, 146.7 with a six-month bonus and 171.8 with a twelve-month bonus; the retirement hazard at age 60 rose from .193 to .364 (ratio 1.89). Lumsdaine, Stock & Wise (1990), 'Efficient windows and labor force reduction', Journal of Public Economics 43(2), 131-159 (NBER Working Paper 3369). Range: the six-month (1.61) to twelve-month (1.89) plans.

drp_window_months.source: The offer paid employees until 30 September 2025, 7.5 months after it closed on 12 February 2025 (OPM, 'Fork in the road' email of 28 January 2025). Upper end: the twelve-month window of Lumsdaine, Stock & Wise (1990). Months of normal voluntary leaving that the offer can capture.

drp_capture.source: Authored: the share of employees who would have left voluntarily within the window anyway and take the paid offer instead, leaving on 30 September rather than at their planned date. It moves departures in time and does not change their total, which the window multiplier sets. No published estimate; the full range is used.

drp_reach.source: Authored: share of full-time employees to whom the offer applied. OPM's email of 28 January 2025 offered deferred resignation 'to all full-time federal employees except for military personnel of the armed forces, employees of the U.S. Postal Service, those in positions related to immigration enforcement and national security, and those in any other positions specifically excluded by your employing agency'; no count of excluded positions was published when the offer was made. The scenario offers it to full-time twins only.

takeaways: From 2025-02 to 2025-12, the simulation's error in each agency's monthly separations was 46.3% (accuracy 53.7%), against 55.7% for the best series method (Same month last year).
The programme calculation that applies the same published effects to whole agencies was at 40.9%.
Total separations: actual 366,779, simulation 245,532, Same month last year 203,364.
